bibl.title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
bibl.publisher: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: As such, the present paper is a conceptual discussion of how to best integrate AI in the classroom, focusing on higher education.

span.label: AI integration in classroom teaching
span.quote: This article delves into the multifaceted role of AI in the classroom, focusing particularly on the primacy of prompt engineering, AI literacy, and the cultivation of critical thinking skills.

span.label: review
span.quote: This is discussed through a case-study based on a Swiss university and a narrative literature review, followed by practical suggestions of how to implement AI in the classroom.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: odd prompt phrases such as "take a deep breath" work because that wording is statistically associated with more nuanced behaviour in the model's internet training data
span.quote: Most likely, this may have to do with the fact that in its training material (which nota bene incorporates large portions of the publicly available internet data) this statement is associated with more nuanced behaviors.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Tree-of-Thought improves answers by combining chain-of-thought with self-consistency so the model can backtrack across reasoning lines and converge on the best one
span.quote: ToT uses a combination of CoT and SC-prompting and builds on this the idea that one can go back and forth, eventually converging on the best line of reasoning.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: prompt design fosters critical thinking by forcing students to take multiple perspectives on a problem and to analyse and construct solutions rather than receive them
span.quote: By carefully designing prompts, educators can encourage students to approach problems from different perspectives, analyze information critically, and develop solutions creatively.

span.label: The discussion is pitched at higher education and adult students; its applicability to children is asserted rather than shown.
span.quote: While this means that it may predominantly be relevant for adult students, it is believed that it may be useful for children as well.

span.label: Two opposite institutional policies on the same technology are presented side by side.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about how education is responding to these tools: the paper sets out that some institutions have banned their use for theses and papers while others have fully allowed it with no or only little limitations
span.quote: some educational institutions have banned their use for students’ theses and papers Upon the introduction of capable LLMs such as ChatGPT, some institutions have fully allowed their students to use them for their academic papers and tasks with no or only little limitations

span.label: A named risk of the technology is that its users do not know its limitations.
span.note: what this limits: any classroom use of these systems described here: the authors list teachers and students not being aware of the limitations and dangers of the technology, giving false responses through AI hallucinations as the example
span.quote: Both teachers and students not being aware of the limitations and dangers of the technology (i.e. generating false responses through AI hallucinations

span.label: extends → Chan (2023)
span.quote: Whereas previous papers have already hinted at the importance of recognizing the relevance of AI in the classroom and suggested preliminary frameworks (Chan, 2023), the present discussion claims that there are three prime skills necessary for the future of education in an AI-adopted world.

span.label: AI hallucinations —causes→ false responses
span.quote: Both teachers and students not being aware of the limitations and dangers of the technology (i.e. generating false responses through AI hallucinations

span.label: The paper's central claim is that three specific skills - AI literacy, prompt engineering knowledge and critical thinking - are what schools need to remedy the problems AI creates in education.
span.quote: In order for all parties to be best prepared for using AI in education, based on a case study and a subsequent literature analysis, there are three necessary skills that can remedy these problems, which are AI literacy, knowledge about prompt engineering, and critical thinking.

span.label: In the author's own trial, GPT-3.5 answered a lost-object reasoning task incorrectly under plain input-output prompting but correctly under Tree-of-Thought prompting.
span.quote: The present author’s experiments have indicated that GPT-3.5 provides false answers to this task when asked with Input–Output prompting. However, the responses turned out to be correct when asked with ToT-prompting.

span.label: The case-study university settled on a middle-ground policy in which student use of ChatGPT and other LLMs is neither banned nor left unrestricted.
span.quote: For the members of the AI-Taskforce and the university’s leadership, this has come to mean that the use of ChatGPT and other LLMs are neither prohibited nor allowed without restrictions.

span.label: Requiring students to document how they critically evaluated the AI's output was the element of the guidelines the authors considered novel relative to other institutions.
span.quote: This is why we considered our third point in the documentation requirements (the need for critical reflection) our most crucial innovation – something that we did not find in other schools and universities.

span.label: The written AI guidelines are undermined because they work only if students voluntarily read and follow them, and compliance cannot be verified.
span.quote: One of the most substantial issues is the fact that their effectiveness hinges on student compliance, which is not guaranteed.

span.label: The main barrier to teachers adopting AI tools in class is fear rooted in not knowing enough about the technology and expecting to use it wrongly.
span.quote: Discussions with teachers have shown that one of the biggest constraints to implement AI tools in the classroom is their fear of using them, predominantly due to the fact that they might not know enough about them and assuming that they might use them wrongly.

span.label: A year after ChatGPT's release, almost all students in the case-study classrooms had already used it.
span.quote: Discussions with students in the classroom at KFH have shown that one year after the introduction of ChatGPT, only few have not yet used it.

span.label: The institution has nobody formally responsible for tracking AI developments, leaving it to individual staff on their own time.
span.quote: One of the marked challenges at the KFH is the ostensible fact that there is no dedicated person or group that is tasked with staying on top of the matter.

span.label: The university offers no workshops or training programmes to raise teacher or student competence with AI.
span.quote: at KFH there are currently no workshops and programs helping both teachers and students to improve in these matters

span.label: AI literacy
span.quote: It encompasses not just the technical know-how but also an awareness of the ethical and societal implications of AI.

span.label: prompt engineering
span.quote: Prompt engineering, at its core, involves the strategic crafting of inputs to elicit desired responses or behaviors from AI systems.

span.label: critical thinking (in the context of AI education)
span.term: critical thinking (in the context of AI education)
span.quote: Critical thinking, in the context of AI education, involves the ability to analyze information, evaluate different perspectives, and create reasoned arguments, all within the framework of AI-driven environments.

span.label: Few-Shot prompting
span.quote: Few-Shot prompting is a technique where a prompt is enriched with several examples of how the task should be completed.

span.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting
span.quote: This is referred to as Chainof-Thought (CoT) prompting where the machine is asked to explain the reasoning steps that lead to a certain outcome.

span.label: expert prompting (EP)
span.quote: The idea is that the model should assume the role of an expert (whereas first the role of the expert is explained in detail) and then the result is generated from an expert’s perspective.

span.label: AI Lock-In problem
span.quote: AI Lock-In problem: An AI can get stuck within a certain narrative and thus loses the full picture

span.label: prompt-wise tabula-rasa problem
span.quote: This is here referred to as the prompt-wise tabula-rasa problem, since it feels like one is sitting in front a “white paper” with no clue how to best start.

span.label: ToT-context
span.quote: This context is what can be called the ToT-context, which applies regardless of the specific task.

span.label: universal and transferrable prompt suffix
span.quote: Such general addendums that can be added to any prompt to improve the results are sometimes referred to as a “universal and transferrable prompt suffix”, which is frequently employed as a method to successfully jailbreak an LLM

span.label: Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE)
span.quote: The APE starts out with one or several examples (of text, music, images, or anything else the model can work with) with the goal to ask the AI which prompts would work best to generate these

span.label: prompting method (Input-Output versus Tree-of-Thought)
span.quote: The present author’s experiments have indicated that GPT-3.5 provides false answers to this task when asked with Input–Output prompting. However, the responses turned out to be correct when asked with ToT-prompting.

span.label: correctness of the model's answer to the reasoning task
span.term: correctness of the model's answer to the reasoning task
span.quote: The present author’s experiments have indicated that GPT-3.5 provides false answers to this task when asked with Input–Output prompting. However, the responses turned out to be correct when asked with ToT-prompting.
